answer: Each new agent must build a persistent reputation by completing randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks before it can influence high-value decisions. Evaluators stake tokens on their judgments and lose them when audits expose collusion, while an agent’s history cannot be transferred to a fresh identity. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund many accounts, wait through the same garden of probation tasks, and risk slashed stakes; cheap identities alone cannot buy influence, even at the zenith of a basalt market.
